text: In my family, we bury our dead with a stone in their mouth.
When I was eight, I watched Gran do it to Grandad.
She said, the dead wake up hungry.
They chew their shroud. Thread by thread.
And while they chew... the family dies. One by one.
Gran's been gone for years.
Last month, there was another funeral in our family.
Small. Rainy. Mum doesn't believe in the old ways.
There was no stone.
A week later, my uncle died in his sleep.
Then my aunt.
I've been so tired. I can't seem to get up.
Tonight, I woke at three. My jaw ached.
Something was chewing. Slow. Close.
I told myself it was coming from the grave.
Then I felt thread between my teeth.
I turned on the torch.
White satin. Six inches above my face.
It was my funeral.
Mum's texted again.
She's the last one left.
Still hungry.
